generated_summary: Many countries where neglected tropical diseases are common cannot start or expand health programs because they lack the baseline data needed for planning and advocacy. To address this, researchers developed the Integrated Threshold Mapping (ITM) methodology to simultaneously map lymphatic filariasis, trachoma, schistosomiasis, and soil-transmitted helminths. The specific purpose of this protocol is to determine if a disease has reached the threshold for public health intervention rather than providing exact prevalence figures. The team tested the protocol by comparing it to standard WHO mapping methodologies in one district each in Mali and Senegal. The ITM methodology reached the same conclusions as the standard methods for most diseases but resulted in more targeted intervention recommendations for schistosomiasis. The study found that the integrated approach was feasible and led to a 31% cost savings in Mali and a 19% cost savings in Senegal. This new tool is more efficient in its use of transport, time in the field, and human resources compared to non-integrated methods.
